summary: Created a 6-phase plan for the picker sync allow-list skills defect covering scope items A-E: scratch-tree reproduction (hard gate), category shape survey, generalized post-filter, wipeout detector, regression spec, and one deliberate redeploy. Corrected one research claim: the 'subdir == filter_category' invariant is false for OpenCode agents (agents_subdir == 'agent/subagents'), so the fix anchors on subdir with a basename fallback rather than on filter_category as research recommended. Effort 4.5 hours across 5 dependency waves.
decisions_made: Anchor the generalized allow-list match on the sync_scan subdir argument, not filter_category, because they diverge for OpenCode agents (agents_subdir == 'agent/subagents') and anchoring on filter_category would silently drop every OpenCode agent
Require a basename fallback when the generalized match fails, so a future divergent call site degrades to today's behavior instead of wiping a category
Escape the interpolated subdir with vim.pesc() before building the Lua pattern
Phase 1 reproduction is a hard gate: if skills do not come back zero, stop and record that the diagnosis did not hold rather than forcing the fix
Zero-result detector triggers only on total wipeout (#results>0 and #filtered==0), non-blocking WARN via helpers.notify
Add a new sync_spec.lua regression spec following the existing scan_spec.lua scratch-tree convention
Keep scripts/tests and scripts/lint absence from provides.scripts out of scope; record as a follow-up candidate
Leave docs/templates/systemd unfiltered as they are today
dead_ends: Research's recommended anchor on filter_category was rejected after verifying agents_subdir resolves to 'agent/subagents' for base_dir == '.opencode' in shared/extensions/config.lua
